title: Summoned to play for Atatürk in Ankara
summary: A Turkish officer told Lehmann the President wanted the orchestra in Ankara the next day despite the hotel gala, and warned that refusal meant never leaving Turkey.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: because I'd seen him in London, and I'd seen him -- he was much older than I was, you know. I saw him in England, and I was glad to be meeting him in Turkey. And we had a very nice time. He had a very fine show, and there was no problem, until one evening playing at the Petite Chaut in Paris itself, Mr. Lehmann sent for me to come to his office. I went to his office and there was an officer, a Turkish officer, and he said to me, he said, "Mr. Briggs, tomorrow we have a very, very big gala evening." I said, "Yes." I said, "We're rehearsed and everything. The show is rehearsed." He said, "Yes, but that's not the point." He said, "I have a command by the President of the Republic, Kemal Attaturk Pasha, asking to send my orchestra to Ankara, tomorrow." He said, "But you can't make it." I said, "I have nothing to do with it. But, you --". You see, I saw right away
that I'd be on the spot.
That the blame would be on me.
So I said, 'No, Mr. Lehmann, we're not responsible.' I said, 'You have your big gala event tomorrow, and it would be awful if you had to send the band away.'

So, the officer who hadn't said a word so far, and he spoke perfect English naturally, and French, he said, 'Yes, but there's no question of disobeying the President.' 'The President wants the band and you must accept.'
And this was in Ankara. He wanted you to come to Ankara, 'cause he wanted you to work.
And the point was, the hotel where you were playing, they were having a big evening, themselves?
And finally, he said, he said, "Well," he said, "I'm going to decide," the officer said, "I'm going to take the decision myself."

He said, "You shall stay here." "You and the orchestra will stay here after your work. We'll take you to your hotels. You can sleep, and we'll awaken you early in the morning and at 10:00 we will take you to Ankara."
There was nothing we could do.
me and he said, "Well," -- he spoke French, and he looked at me and he said, "Je parle enfer." (?) I said, "Non." (Laughter).
So, it happened that way that the next morning, and the orchestra wasn't so satisfied, but we had no choice.

Oh yes, the orchestra, he added, he said, "There's only one other thing that will happen to you if you refuse to go." "We can't force you to go. But if you do refuse to go, you'll never leave Turkey." (Laughter). "You'll have to stay in Turkey for the rest of your days."
